$doc: Review queue (designed 2026-10-05): approvals queue one apply at a time per vault; after each apply waiting batches are re-checked and stale ones rebuilt (unapproved: before the owner looks; approved: rebuilt, then one more OK, decision A); exit 75 reads Updating, never a failure; bounded self-recovery (rules first, then a recovery model, default Opus); the batch tabs become a left list. states.label: A · The batch list: readable names, date, sources, one state, oldest first; Approve says it queues
B · Queued: applies after the batch being added; checked against the pages before it goes in
C · Not approved yet and stale: rebuilt by its own session before you look (Updating…)
D · Approved but stale: rebuilt, keeps its place, one more OK with What changed since you approved
E · Stale again: rebuilt in its session first, then Recovering · Opus; one notice, one attempts line
F · Distill couldn’t fix this: What was tried (one row per attempt), Rebuild against the latest pages, Let recovery try again, Continue in a new session (proposed), Open in Terminal, Reject batch
G · Claude was blocked from a command: Distill tells it to read the files instead, and it goes on
H · Last resort: what Claude wanted, in plain words; the command only behind Show command
I · Plan error: the fixed reply came first; Recovering · Opus · asking Claude to rebuild the plan
J · Waiting: Recovering · next try at 4:41 PM; a minute between agent attempts
K · A failed batch (runner-failed) gave up: it stays in Review; What was tried, Rebuild, Let recovery try again, Open in Terminal, Reject batch
L · Recovery suggests a new session: the owner confirms in the card (Continue), never automatic
M · Recovery proposes a split: “Rebuild 1 source first” approves only that source; the rest wait
N · Recovery proposes discarding the rebuilt part: “Discard the rebuilt part” rejects the part, never the batch

boards.title: Review queue · approve several, they go in one at a time
boards.heading: Approve as many batches as you like: Distill adds them one at a time and keeps every plan current
boards.intro: “it is very bad, it list out each batch much better” and “when the issue happen it is nearly very difficult for the user to recover or fix the issue by itself, it will keep rerun and nothing will fix”. Approving a batch while another is being added queues it; applies run one at a time per vault, oldest approval first. After each apply the core re-checks every waiting batch against the vault. A stale batch is always rebuilt in its own session first; one you haven’t approved is rebuilt by its own session before you look (Updating…). A stale batch you approved is rebuilt and asks once more, with what changed since you approved: the approval gate binds every byte, so it never carries over (decision A). Exit 75 is never shown as a failure. A batch that still can’t move gets a bounded recovery: rules first, then a recovery model (Opus by default, set in Settings) that picks one fix the core can run and check, at most 2 times and $1.00, then “Distill couldn’t fix this” with your options. Review’s tabs become a list.
